# The Overscan symbol register

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_icons.py from tools/icons.py. Do not edit. -->

An icon set where every mark has a **number** and a **stated meaning**, rather than a bag of glyphs.

The precedent is Ron Cobb's Semiotic Standard, and the precedent is all that transfers. 🔴 **The artwork, the names and the trademarks are not ours to relicense** - the vectorisations in circulation are CC BY 4.0, and upstream is explicit that this does not extend to Cobb's originals or the film material. The idea was the valuable half anyway, and these are authored here.

## The rule

⭐ **The frame is the category and the mark is the meaning.**

That is *decoration needs a rule* applied to iconography, and it buys the set a property almost no icon font has: an unfamiliar symbol is still half-readable, because the triangle tells you it is a hazard before you have worked out what is inside it. The number says the same thing - its tens digit is the category - so a symbol referred to by number alone is also half-understood.

Because both the frame and the number carry the category, they can be **checked against each other**, and they are: `tools/gen_icons.py` refuses to emit if any symbol has drifted out of its family.

## The eight families

The first five report on a MACHINE: what it is doing (state), what will hurt you (hazard), which part of it you are looking at (system), what is moving through it (flow), and what you may do to it (action).

The last three are about the SHIP AND THE PEOPLE IN IT, which is the half of the precedent a console-only set leaves out and the half that is actually painted on bulkheads: where you are and how you get out (wayfinding), what is required of the person standing here (crew), and what the hardware needs from whoever services it (maintenance).

🔴 **Two digits ceils the set at nine families of nine.** Eight families are spent and the ninth tens digit is deliberately left unspent, because a register that fills its own numbering the moment it can has no room to be wrong about a category later. A TENTH family is not a new row in the register, it is a different numbering scheme, and `check()` refuses rather than letting that happen quietly.

## Modifiers

⭐ **A diagonal slash negates the symbol it crosses**, in any category. Having exactly one such mark is what keeps it readable: `14 offline` is a state negated and `44 blocked` is a flow negated, and neither has to be learned separately once the slash is.

⭐ **A horizontal dash inside a frame means absence.** `15 no reading` is a state with nothing in it; `25 vacuum` is a space with nothing in it. Not a collision: the frame already said which kind of absence.

## Sub-rules, which are not modifiers

A modifier means one thing everywhere. These two mean something only INSIDE their family, so they are written down separately rather than smuggled in as a third and fourth modifier.

⭐ **In the state circle, how much of the dot is filled is how much of the thing is working.** Filled is `11 nominal`, half is `17 degraded`, hollow is `16 standby`. Three symbols, one gradient, nothing to memorise.

⭐ **In the flow channel, the line and the chevrons carry the rate.** A dashed line is `49 trickle`, a single chevron is the ordinary case, and a doubled chevron is `48 surge`. Rate is drawn, not labelled.

## Construction

24x24 grid, stroke 2, butt caps, miter joins, `currentColor` throughout so a symbol takes the theme like everything else. Nothing is filled except where filling is the distinction (`11 nominal` against `15 no reading`).

⚠️ **A frame that tapers has a wedge for an interior, not a box.** Two passes at the hazard marks failed on this: the first drew them too small to read at 30px, and the second drew four-stroke marks sized for a box, which came out as a bowtie, a bolt crossing its own frame, and spokes leaving the bottom edge. Hazard marks are two or three bold strokes, sat low where the wedge is wide. The shield has the same problem upside down, so crew marks stay clear of its tip.

⚠️ **A mark can read as a letter, or as a bowtie.** `39 structure` was an X between two rails, which collapses to an hourglass, and `37 navigation` was a notched arrowhead, which is a capital A no matter how deep the notch is cut. The fixes generalise: a beam section cannot collapse, and a SOLID shape cannot be a letterform, because letterforms are strokes.

## A mark never crowds its frame

⭐ The frame carries the category, so it has to survive being looked at quickly, and a mark run up against the frame edge fuses with it. `tools/clearance.py` measures the visible gap on every symbol - flattening frame and mark to point clouds, taking the closest approach, and subtracting the stroke each actually paints - and refuses if any symbol is tight.

⭐ **The margin is one ninth of the room the frame has.** One absolute number is the obvious rule and it is wrong, because the frames are not the same size inside: the state circle holds an inscribed disc of 9.00 and the hazard triangle holds 5.40, so a figure generous enough for the circle shrinks hazard marks back to the size that already failed a pass. Every frame gives up the same PROPORTION of its interior instead, with the roomiest frame setting the constant at 1.00.

## There is no fallback glyph

🔴 Asking for a name the register does not define gets a **refusal**, not a question mark and not a nearest match. A fallback would be the display inventing a meaning nobody assigned, which is the same failure as a seven-segment readout closing the gap on `1.5`. Symbol **00** is reserved for saying the register has no answer and is not a symbol in the set.

`OverscanIcons.means(name)` answers with the sentence below, or `null`. Never with a guess.

## The register

### state &mdash; a condition of the thing being reported on

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **11** | `nominal` | reading is within its declared range and current |
| **12** | `caution` | reading is real and outside its comfortable band |
| **13** | `fault` | the thing reporting is broken, not the reading |
| **14** | `offline` | nothing is reporting and nothing is expected to |
| **15** | `no reading` | no value has arrived. deliberately a dash, which is the refusal idiom the segment readouts use, and deliberately not a zero |
| **16** | `standby` | powered, correct, and doing nothing. the hollow dot is the empty end of the fill ladder that 11 fills and 17 half-fills |
| **17** | `degraded` | running, and not at full capability. ⭐ the half-filled dot is the middle of the ladder, so the three states are one gradient rather than three unrelated marks |
| **18** | `stale` | a value did arrive and is too old to be trusted. ⭐ NOT the same as 15: this one has a number to show you and is telling you not to believe it |
| **19** | `projected` | this value was computed forward, not measured. ⭐ the solid dot is the last real reading and the dashes are what comes after it, because a readout that refuses to invent still has to be allowed to extrapolate OUT LOUD. ⚠️ the first drawing was a solid line going dashed as it rose, and a diagonal inside the state circle is 14 offline - a mark cannot borrow the negation slash to mean something that is not negation |

### hazard &mdash; a danger present at this location

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **21** | `pressure` | pressure differential across this boundary |
| **22** | `thermal` | surface or medium at a harmful temperature |
| **23** | `electrical` | live conductor present |
| **24** | `radiation` | ionising source |
| **25** | `vacuum` | this space is or may become unpressurised. the dash is the same absence mark 15 carries, and the frame is what says which kind |
| **26** | `corrosive` | a substance here attacks what it touches, including you |
| **27** | `contaminated` | the atmosphere here is present and must not be breathed. ⭐ the mark is 34 atmosphere wearing the slash, which is the whole system working: a borrowed mark and a known modifier, read in the frame that says danger |

### system &mdash; a subsystem, named rather than described

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **31** | `power` | electrical supply |
| **32** | `comms` | signal link to somewhere else |
| **33** | `coolant` | heat transfer loop |
| **34** | `atmosphere` | breathable supply and its handling |
| **35** | `storage` | held material or held data |
| **36** | `propulsion` | thrust, and the machinery that makes it |
| **37** | `navigation` | where the vehicle is and where it is pointed. ⚠️ drawn as an outline this is a capital A, and deepening the notch does not help because the SILHOUETTE is what reads as the letter. filling it does: letterforms are strokes, so a solid shape cannot be one. same class of mistake as the bowtie 39 had to be redrawn out of |
| **38** | `compute` | processing, and the machine that does it. the mark is a clock because a clock is the part of a computer you can actually point at |
| **39** | `structure` | hull, frame, and whatever everything else is bolted to. ⚠️ drawn first as a braced bay, which is an X between two rails and therefore a BOWTIE at size - the same mistake the hazard marks already cost a pass. a beam section is the thing itself and cannot collapse |

### flow &mdash; something moving through a channel

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **41** | `intake` | flow entering the system here |
| **42** | `exhaust` | flow leaving the system here |
| **43** | `circulate` | flow returning to where it came from |
| **44** | `blocked` | flow that cannot pass. ⚠️ the first drawing was 41 with the wall doubled, and at 30px the two were indistinguishable - which is a real failure in a set whose whole claim is that you can read it. it now carries the slash, the same negation 14 carries |
| **45** | `vent` | flow released to the outside, on purpose |
| **46** | `leak` | flow leaving the channel where nothing was meant to leave. ⭐ 45 is the same event authorised, and keeping them apart is most of why this register exists |
| **47** | `filtered` | flow passes, and something is taken out of it on the way |
| **48** | `surge` | flow above its rated rate. the doubled chevron is the fast end of the rate ladder 49 sits at the slow end of |
| **49** | `trickle` | flow present and below its rated rate. ⭐ the broken line is the rate, drawn rather than labelled - which is the same argument as the fill ladder in the state circle |

### action &mdash; an operation the reader can perform

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **51** | `engage` | start, and keep running |
| **52** | `hold` | suspend without releasing the state |
| **53** | `purge` | empty this, discarding what is in it |
| **54** | `isolate` | break the connection and leave both sides intact |
| **55** | `override` | proceed past a refusal. the only symbol in the set for doing something the system has already declined, so it is deliberately not comfortable |
| **56** | `abort` | stop now and do not resume. 52 keeps the state and this one does not |
| **57** | `reset` | return to the declared starting state. ⚠️ the head is solid because a stroked one left a ring with a nub, and a ring with a nub is 31 power |
| **58** | `acknowledge` | you have seen it, and it stops asking. ⭐ it does not stop being true, which is why this is not the same control as 56 |
| **59** | `step` | advance exactly one increment and stop. ⚠️ 51 with a wall added, which is the 41-against-44 shape of mistake - it survives only because the transport idiom is already learned everywhere, and it was checked against 51 at 30px before it was kept |

### wayfinding &mdash; a place, and the way into or out of it

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **61** | `airlock` | a chamber with a door at each end, to be passed one at a time |
| **62** | `hatch` | a single closure that can be dogged shut against pressure |
| **63** | `ladder` | a route between decks, climbed |
| **64** | `corridor` | a route along this deck, walked |
| **65** | `deck` | a level. the long stroke is the one you are standing on |
| **66** | `muster station` | where people gather when something has gone wrong. ⭐ it is 71 crew present, twice, read in the frame that means A PLACE - which is the clearest case in the set of the frame doing the work |
| **67** | `exit` | the way out of this space, in an emergency |
| **68** | `position` | you are here. the only symbol in the set that means something different depending on where it is printed, which is why it is a pin and not a dot |
| **69** | `restricted` | a doorway you may not go through. the slash is the same negation 14, 44 and 76 carry |

### crew &mdash; something required of the person standing here

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **71** | `crew present` | this space is occupied |
| **72** | `suit required` | do not be here without a pressure suit. ⚠️ the visor was first a chord across a circle, which is the 15 absence dash wearing a different frame and therefore already spoken for |
| **73** | `eye protection` | do not be here without eye protection |
| **74** | `hearing protection` | do not be here without hearing protection |
| **75** | `medical` | treatment, and the people qualified to give it |
| **76** | `unmanned` | nobody is meant to be in here. ⭐ it is the crew figure negated, so a person in this space is the anomaly rather than the default |

### maintenance &mdash; hardware, and the servicing it expects

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **81** | `fastener` | a bolted joint. ⭐ a bolt says THIS FACE IS FIXED, which is exactly what stops the bolts on a rack faceplate being decoration |
| **82** | `seal` | a gasket or ring that is consumed by being opened, and is replaced rather than reused |
| **83** | `filter element` | a consumable that gets dirty on purpose so nothing downstream does |
| **84** | `fuse` | a part that is meant to fail, so that the expensive part does not |
| **85** | `calibration point` | where an instrument is told what true is. ⭐ every readout in this kit that refuses to invent a value is relying on somebody having come here |
| **86** | `lockout` | deliberately dead for servicing, and not to be re-energised by anyone who did not kill it. the most important mark in this family |

### reserved

| | name | means |
|---:|---|---|
| **00** | `unregistered` | reserved. no symbol is defined for the name that was asked for, and one is not invented |
